body:
REMOTE-CONSOLE DESIGN — origin and data-plane boundary

Recommendation: deploy two actual web origins, not only two routes:
- https://display.example.com — public presentation runtime; host-only Secure HttpOnly SameSite=Strict cookie; can receive public state and send only display receipts/health.
- https://console.example.com — Presenter Console; separate host-only cookie; can receive private state and issue typed commands.
- Each origin exposes its own same-origin `/api/*` and `/socket` BFF/proxy into an internal session service. Never set `Domain=.example.com`; never place bearer tokens in WebSocket query strings. Exact Origin allowlisting occurs at both edge and WebSocket upgrade. This is practical behind one CDN/load balancer and creates meaningful cookie, service-worker, DOM, CSP and BroadcastChannel boundaries. A distinct hostname alone is insufficient if parent-domain cookies or a shared overly broad backend ACL remain.

Server-side topic ACL (no client-side filtering):
1. `s/{sid}/public.state` — publisher: session service only; subscribers: display + presenter. Contract contains only `{slideId, buildStep, blackout, publicMedia, themeRevision}`.
2. `s/{sid}/presenter.private` — publisher: session service only; subscriber: presenter only. `{speakerNotes, nextSlidePreview, privateTimer, backstageMessages}`. It is never serialized for a display connection.
3. `s/{sid}/control.commands` — publisher: active presenter lease only; consumer: session service only. Typed allowlist such as `slide.set`, `slide.next`, `build.next`, `blackout.set`, `timer.start`; never arbitrary topic names or JSON patches.
4. `s/{sid}/control.receipts` — publisher: service/display; subscriber: presenter. Accepted/rejected/applied receipts, no notes.
5. `s/{sid}/display.receipts` — publisher: display only; service consumes; fields only `{commandId, revision, renderMs, result}`.
6. `s/{sid}/presenter.presence` — service to presenter only; device/lease diagnostics. Display gets, at most, one public boolean `controllerConnected` if product wants it.

Authorization tuple on every inbound frame: `{tenantId, sessionId, role, connectionId, controllerEpoch}` derived from the authenticated socket, never trusted from JSON. Broker subscriptions are materialized server-side from role; clients cannot SUBSCRIBE to arbitrary strings. The audience/display application has no code path or schema for `presenter.private`. Add a contract/integration assertion: authenticating as DISPLAY and requesting private topic returns `403 topic_forbidden`, and a complete display socket capture contains no private-schema field names or values.

Separate-origin trade-off: costs another deployment/CORS/BFF configuration and prevents BroadcastChannel across console/display by design; benefits are decisive because an XSS/service-worker compromise in public display origin cannot read presenter cookies/storage or join presenter BroadcastChannels. RFC 6454 defines origins and the Origin header: https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6454 . Current cookie draft specifies the `__Host-` prefix as Secure, Path=/, no Domain: https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-ietf-httpbis-rfc6265bis . WHATWG says BroadcastChannel is for browsing contexts of a given origin, not devices: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/dev/web-messaging.html#broadcasting-to-other-browsing-contexts .

## EXPAND
- LEAD: If fully offline operation is mandatory, investigate managed local relay certificate provisioning; automatic fallback to cleartext LAN WebSocket is not acceptable.
- LEAD: Decide whether anonymous pairing is allowed; if yes, display-local approval/SAS is a security requirement because a public QR is observable by the audience.
